verdict.rationale: Meilisearch is explicitly a single binary with no external dependencies that can be self-hosted on Linux/macOS/Windows/bare-metal/containers, confirmed by a hands-on runtime probe showing successful install and a real search roundtrip, and community reports confirm production self-hosted use at scale (k8s, Hetzner, millions of docs). However, one Cloud-only feature (Read High Availability/clusterization) is advertised specifically for the hosted product, and production self-hosting requires manual setup of reverse proxy, process manager, and master key rather than being fully turnkey; community reports also note RAM unpredictability and indexing lag under heavy write load. Missing for 10: confirmation that all Cloud-exclusive features (HA/clustering, some analytics/personalization) are actually available in the open-source self-hosted binary, and independent large-scale ops benchmarks beyond anecdotal HN reports.
